title: Taiwan’s Local Elections Are Not About China, President Lai, or the United States
gist: Lev Nachman argues that Taiwan's November 2026 local elections for mayors, councilors and village chiefs should not be read as a verdict on China, President Lai Ching-te, Trump or war risk, because local elections turn on local issues. Split-ticket evidence, such as KMT mayors in Taichung and New Taipei whose voters still backed Lai and the DPP in 2024, shows local results do not predict national preferences.

themes.theme: Misreading local elections as geopolitical referendums

insights.claim: Reading Taiwan's November local election results as a verdict on Taiwanese attitudes toward China, President Lai Ching-te, Trump or a potential war would be an analytical mistake, because the outcomes cannot be explained by national issues like independence or unification.
insights.so_what: Investors and analysts should avoid over-interpreting a KMT local win as a pro-Beijing shift or a DPP loss as weakening Taiwan's China policy; cross-strait risk signals lie elsewhere.
insights.quote: That would be an analytical mistake.
insights.speaker: Lev Nachman

insights.claim: Decades of data show Taiwanese voters prioritize China, sovereignty and Taiwan's future in national elections, but there is little longitudinal data on how they decide in local ones.
insights.so_what: The evidence base for inferring national sentiment from local votes is thin, so conclusions drawn from local results carry high uncertainty.

insights.claim: Taichung and New Taipei elected Kuomintang mayors in each of the last two local elections, yet a majority of their voters supported Lai and the Democratic Progressive Party in the 2024 presidential election.
insights.so_what: Party control of big cities is a poor predictor of presidential outcomes, so a KMT local sweep would not necessarily foreshadow a change in Taiwan's national leadership.

insights.claim: Legislator Su Chiao-hui is running for New Taipei City mayor and opened a joint campaign headquarters with councilor Chang Chin-hao in Xizhi District in September 2026.
insights.so_what: New Taipei, Taiwan's most populous city and a KMT-held seat, is a race that foreign observers are likely to over-read nationally.
